# tools-computers

The tools that use a computer: computer_list, computer_view, computer_windows, computer_pointer, computer_keyboard, computer_clipboard, computer_tools, computer_call and computer_use. Each names the computer it acts on, or leaves it to the session's preference, and the fixed vocabulary is what a computer's MCP server answers.

- **Runs in:** the harness process
- **Source:** [lisp/modules/harness-tools-computers.el](../../lisp/modules/harness-tools-computers.el)
- **Loaded:** by default
- **Requires:** [computers](computers.md), [tools](tools.md)

## About

A session is not on a computer: it uses the tools of the computers
it may reach (see harness-computers.el).  These are the tools:

  computer_list      the computers, their state, capabilities and
                     resources, and what this session may use;
  computer_view      a screen capture of the desktop or one window;
  computer_windows   the windows of the desktop;
  computer_pointer   move, click, scroll and drag;
  computer_keyboard  type text and press keys;
  computer_clipboard read and write the clipboard;
  computer_tools     the extra tools this computer's implementation
                     offers, beyond the fixed vocabulary;
  computer_call      call one of those extra tools;
  computer_use       which computer a call names when it names none.

The fixed vocabulary is the computer-use interface, and what a
computer answers is its implementation's MCP server, reached over the
ACP connection of the client running there.  Each tool names a
computer (`:computer`), or leaves it to the session's preference; each
says which capability it needs, and the permission chain's computer
gate (a stage at 7) refuses, for good, a call to a computer the
session may not use, one whose grant does not hold the capability, or
one that drives a computer a person has taken control of.  The
handler checks the same thing again, for a call the permission chain
did not see (`tools/execute-approved`).

Not every computer has every capability, and none may be registered
at all: a call says why and what to do about it, and the model is
meant to tell the user and ask for a computer with
`request_escalation` (attribute computer) rather than guess.  A screen
capture comes back as bytes over MCP and is written into the
session's temporary directory here, so the model sees the picture and
the user does wherever the session is shown.

## Provides

### Tools

- `computer_call` — Call one of the extra tools a computer's implementation offers (computer_tools lists them) with its arguments. It needs the capability named in capability (exec by default) and a session grant for it: an extra tool may do anything its implementation says, so treat it as running a program on that computer. Use files for the file tools a computer scopes to its own storage.
- `computer_camera` — Take one picture with a computer's camera. It needs a computer this session may use, with the `camera` capability and a session grant for it; the picture comes back for you to see, and the user sees it in the chat. A computer without a camera, or one whose camera permission is denied, says so.
- `computer_clipboard` — Read (action get) or write (action set, with text) the clipboard of a computer. Needs the `clipboard` capability; writing also waits while a person has control of that computer.
- `computer_keyboard` — Type text or press a key on a computer. Needs the `keyboard` capability and a session grant for it; while a person has control of the computer it waits. Name one window (`window`, from computer_windows) when the implementation is window-scoped.
- `computer_list` — List the computers the harness may use: the ones clients registered, each one's state, computer-use capabilities (view, windows, pointer, keyboard, clipboard, audio, camera, files, sandbox, exec), resources and projects, and whether this session may use it. Call it before using another computer_* tool, and to see what a refusal means; with no computer registered it says so, and the harness still works, as a chat until a client registers a computer.
- `computer_pointer` — Move the pointer, click, scroll or drag on a computer's desktop. Needs the `pointer` capability and a session grant for it; while a person has control of the computer it waits. Prefer acting on one window (`window`, from computer_windows) when the implementation is window-scoped, which is the least access that does the job.
- `computer_tools` — List the extra tools a computer's implementation offers beyond the fixed computer-use vocabulary (view, windows, pointer, keyboard, clipboard, audio), with the server that runs them. Call one with computer_call.
- `computer_use` — Choose the computer this session uses when a call names none, among the computers it may use (computer_list says which). It is a preference, not a grant, and not a pin: a call that names a computer, and a resource of one, still goes where it names. Give no computer to clear it.
- `computer_view` — Look at the screen of a computer: the desktop, or one window it names. The picture comes back for you to see (and for the user, in the chat). It needs a computer this session may use, with the `view` capability; while a person has control of it you may still look, but not type or click. Leave window out for the whole desktop, or name one from computer_windows.
- `computer_windows` — List the windows a computer can see, each with its id, application, title and rectangle. Use the id with computer_view or computer_pointer to act on that one window, which is least privilege when the computer's implementation is window-scoped.
